Let  
\[
s=\sin x,\quad c=\cos x.
\]
Given
\[
s+c=\frac15.
\]
Using \(\sin^2 x+\cos^2 x=1\),
\[
s^2+c^2=1.
\]
Now
\[
(s+c)^2=s^2+c^2+2sc=1+2sc.
\]
So
\[
\left(\frac15\right)^2=1+2sc
\]
\[
\frac1{25}=1+2sc
\]
\[
2sc=\frac1{25}-1=-\frac{24}{25}
\]
\[
sc=-\frac{12}{25}.
\]
Since \(0<x<\pi\), \(\sin x>0\). Also \(sc<0\), so \(\cos x<0\). Thus \(x\) is in quadrant II.

Now \(s\) and \(c\) are roots of
\[
t^2-\frac15t-\frac{12}{25}=0.
\]
Multiplying by \(25\):
\[
25t^2-5t-12=0.
\]
Solving,
\[
t=\frac{5\pm \sqrt{25+1200}}{50}
=\frac{5\pm 35}{50}.
\]
Thus
\[
t=\frac{40}{50}=\frac45
\quad\text{or}\quad
t=\frac{-30}{50}=-\frac35.
\]
Since \(\sin x>0\), \(\sin x=\frac45\), and since \(\cos x<0\), \(\cos x=-\frac35\).

Therefore,
\[
\tan x=\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}
=\frac{\frac45}{-\frac35}
=-\frac43.
\]

The answer is \(-\frac43\).
